headline: Stochastic models link noise and transport to cell-scale outcomes in expression and…
label: Stochastic Cellular Noise Modeling
summary: Recent preprints apply stochastic models to chemotactic migration, gene expression noise, and reaction network dynamics at cellular scales.
synthesis: The dominant thread is stochastic, fluctuation-resolved modeling of cellular processes, in which noise is treated as a model component rather than averaged out. A chemotaxis preprint reports that superdiffusive fractional Brownian motion lets simulated cells reach global chemoattractant maxima robustly. A gene expression preprint shows that protein sequestration modulates expression noise, with non-cooperative binding yielding gamma distributions with reduced noise. A spectral Koopman framework for stochastic reaction networks offers low-dimensional representations with error estimates. What is distinct across these items is the use of noise-shaped outcomes, such as robust migration and altered expression distributions, as the principal readout of the model. The shared element is the stochastic formalism applied at the cellular scale, not a single physical setting.
